candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0161.

options.A: Tell the client that the symptoms indicate nitrate allergy and that all future nitrate therapy should be avoided regardless of cardiovascular need.
options.B: Encourage the client to stand and walk immediately because remaining seated increases venous pooling and worsens nitrate-related lightheadedness.
options.C: Advise the client to repeat doses continuously until the headache stops because headache indicates that the previous dose was below therapeutic strength.
options.D: Explain that headache and dizziness are recognized nitrate effects, keep the client safe from falls, and continue blood-pressure and symptom monitoring.

candidate.rationale: Nitroglycerin commonly causes headache and can cause dizziness or postural hypotension because of vasodilation. In a hemodynamically stable client, these findings should be recognized and monitored rather than misclassified as allergy; safety precautions are appropriate when lightheadedness occurs.
